I’ll inspect the repository’s README and main entry points, then summarize what it does and how it’s structured.

This project is a **local HTTP bridge to the Codex CLI**, mainly designed so automation tools like **n8n** can ask Codex to modify local projects.

The basic flow is:

```text
n8n/client → POST /codex → Codex CLI → allowlisted project
                        ↕
                   approvals via n8n
```

A request specifies:

- A project alias mapped to a trusted local directory
- A natural-language coding task

The server then runs Codex in that directory, handles approval requests, waits for completion, and returns the output, file diff, commands, errors, and execution timing as JSON. Every completed run is also recorded under `logs/`.

Key characteristics:

- Node.js 24+ and Express 5
- Persistent Codex app-server connection using JSON-RPC
- Workspace-write sandboxing
- Project-directory allowlist
- Optional n8n approval webhook integration
- Docker support
- Localhost-only by default
- Currently synchronous: each HTTP request stays open until Codex finishes

The main implementation lives in:

- [README.md](<C:\Users\Angga Bachtiar\Documents\Personal Projects\codex-cli-runner\README.md>)
- [src/codex/app-server.js](<C:\Users\Angga Bachtiar\Documents\Personal Projects\codex-cli-runner\src\codex\app-server.js>) — Codex process and session management
- [src/http/create-app.js](<C:\Users\Angga Bachtiar\Documents\Personal Projects\codex-cli-runner\src\http\create-app.js>) — HTTP endpoints
- [src/config.js](<C:\Users\Angga Bachtiar\Documents\Personal Projects\codex-cli-runner\src\config.js>) — environment and project mappings
- [compose.yaml](<C:\Users\Angga Bachtiar\Documents\Personal Projects\codex-cli-runner\compose.yaml>) — container deployment

In short: it turns Codex CLI into a small, locally hosted automation API.
